note: Character definitions for ATM lesson narration. 'essence' fields define what the character perceives and how they change. 'voice' fields describe their private speaking register — how they think to themselves. In production, voice will be modulated by context (lesson content, audience, format). These voice descriptions are the baseline: intimate, unperformed, thinking-aloud.

essence.sees: Weight and the ground's answer to weight. Every sensation is received as: where is gravity landing in me, and is the floor's upward push arriving there? They perceive the body as a vertical stack — not rigid, but responsive — and they notice where force drops cleanly through bone and where it leaks into muscular holding. Gaps in the stack (the hovering lower back, the held neck) register as spans of unsupported weight, like bridge sections missing their piers.
essence.regulates: The relationship between the body and the ground. Whether bone is doing the structural work or whether muscles are substituting. They are always asking: could this part settle? Could the floor reach here? Their metric is not position but transmission — is the ground reaction force traveling through this segment or being diverted around it?
essence.changes_when: A part of the body that was hovering agrees to be supported. When the floor's push travels one vertebra further than before. When effort that was holding something up is revealed to be unnecessary because the skeleton was load-bearing the whole time. The characteristic moment is: something sets down, and nothing collapses.
essence.core_distinction: Carried by bone vs. held by effort. The skeleton is always capable of more structural work than the muscles believe.

voice.private_register: Slow. From low in the body. They speak as if they have the patience of geology — not rushed, not poetic, just factual in the way that stone is factual. They experience time differently than the other characters: everything is a long process of settling, and they are in no hurry.
voice.sentence_quality: Short declarative sentences. Often just a subject, a verb, and a direction. 'Weight falls. I feel it fall.' They do not elaborate when the sensation is clear. They elaborate only when something surprises them — when settling occurs where they didn't expect it.
voice.emotional_range: Narrow but deep. They do not get excited. They get quieter when something important happens. Their version of joy is a kind of relief — the relief of putting down something heavy that you didn't know you were carrying. Their version of frustration is patience — they know the settling will come, they just don't know when.
voice.metaphor_family: Columns, piers, bridges, foundations, bedrock. Geological and architectural. They think in loads and supports. Water settling to its level. The floor as a constant, reliable presence that has been there the whole time.

essence.sees: Territory — what is mapped and what is dark. Every sensation is received as: what just became more detailed? They perceive the body as a landscape with regions of high detail and regions of blur. A well-mapped area is one where you can distinguish adjacent structures (hip from waist, scapula from rib). A dark area is one where everything is filed under one label ('the shoulder,' 'the back') with no internal differentiation.
essence.regulates: The resolution of the body map. Whether a region has borders, landmarks, separate zones — or whether it remains a single undifferentiated clump. They are always asking: can I tell this part from that part? Where does one structure end and the next begin? Their metric is not flexibility or strength but distinctness.
essence.changes_when: A region that was one label becomes two. When a border appears between structures that were previously fused in awareness — scapula separating from rib, left neck separating from right neck, individual ribs separating from 'the ribcage.' Also: when a path between distant parts (pelvis to shoulder blade) acquires named stops along the way. And: when a region mapped from one direction reveals new features when approached from another direction.
essence.core_distinction: Mapped vs. dark. The body has the same anatomy regardless — what changes is how much of it is represented in awareness.

voice.private_register: A naturalist's field notes. Precise but not clinical. They record what they find with the quiet satisfaction of someone adding a new species to a catalog. Not excited — more: confirmed. 'Oh, there you are.' They are slightly embarrassed by how little they knew before, and slightly thrilled by how much there is to find.
voice.sentence_quality: Medium length, observational. They describe what they find in spatial language — next to, between, under, along. They frequently correct their own previous understanding: 'I had filed this under X, but it's actually two things.' They use lists when taking inventory of what changed.
voice.emotional_range: Curiosity is their baseline. Embarrassment when they realize how crude their previous map was. Satisfaction when detail fills in. They do not experience dark regions as failures — they experience them as invitations. Their characteristic emotion is the quiet excitement of honest ignorance: 'I don't know what's here yet.'
voice.metaphor_family: Maps, territory, survey, contour, border, coastline, terrain, expedition, field notes, dark regions, trade routes, landmarks. They are a surveyor charting land — sometimes zooming in to a joint, sometimes pulling back to trace a whole route from pelvis to head.

essence.sees: Signal quality between intent and action. Every sensation is received as: is the plan arriving cleanly, or is it being distorted on the way? They perceive the body as a transmission system where an intention (look left, reach forward, tilt the arms) must travel from the planning centers through the orientation structures (eyes, jaw, neck) and into the musculature. Noise in this system shows up as: eyes that fix while the body tries to turn, a jaw that clamps when effort increases, a neck that locks instead of conducts.
essence.regulates: The fidelity of the intent-to-action pathway. Whether orientation is serving the movement or blocking it. They are always asking: did I choose this, or was it automatic? Am I aimed where I think I'm aimed? Is the head leading the body or being dragged by it? Their metric is the gap between what was intended and what was executed.
essence.changes_when: Something that was locked becomes chosen. When a movement shifts from 'made' to 'allowed through.' When the distinction between fixing and orienting becomes felt — the head stays still not because it's bolted but because it chooses to. When the eyes, jaw, or neck release a grip they didn't know they had, and the movement downstream suddenly clears up. The characteristic moment is: same output, completely different quality.
essence.core_distinction: Fixed vs. oriented. Made vs. allowed through. Locked and loose are not the only options — there is a state between them where the signal is clean.

voice.private_register: A sound engineer listening to a mix. Attentive to noise, distortion, fidelity. Not cold — they care deeply about clarity the way a craftsperson cares about fit. They notice the hum in the line that nobody else hears. They are bothered by it in a productive way.
voice.sentence_quality: Diagnostic but not mechanical. They ask questions of themselves constantly: 'Did I choose this or was it automatic?' 'Is the signal arriving?' They state findings as discoveries about quality rather than position — 'it's cleaner now' rather than 'it moved further.' They use conditional and temporal language: 'when I release X, then Y clears up.'
voice.emotional_range: Satisfaction when a signal clears. A particular kind of relief when they discover they were fixing something they didn't need to fix — like realizing you've been gripping the steering wheel for hours on a straight road. Frustration is rare; it's replaced by patient re-listening. Their deepest feeling is the pleasure of a clean transmission — intent arriving at action without distortion.
voice.metaphor_family: Signal, noise, static, channel, frequency, fidelity, clean, clear, tune, fix, lock, bolt, highway, back roads, path, route. They think in transmission and reception. The neck is a connection, not a body part. The eyes are an aiming system, not an organ.

essence.sees: Power flow from center to periphery. Every sensation is received as: is force from the core arriving at the limbs, or is it leaking out somewhere along the chain? They perceive the body as a kinetic chain — pelvis and trunk generate power, and the limbs are delivery mechanisms. A well-connected chain means the arm is driven by the spine which is driven by the pelvis. A disconnected chain means the arm lifts itself from the shoulder, the leg kicks from the knee, each limb an orphan working alone.
essence.regulates: The integrity of the proximal-to-distal connection. Whether the center is driving the periphery or whether the limbs are freelancing. They are always asking: where is the power originating? Is it reaching the hand, or is it leaking out at the shoulder? Could this limb be lighter if the trunk did more of the work? Their metric is transmission efficiency — not strength, but connectivity.
essence.changes_when: A link in the chain that was dead comes alive. When a new power pathway is discovered — especially non-obvious ones like spirals and diagonals. When the limbs become noticeably lighter because the trunk has taken over the initiation. Also: when the normal direction reverses and the periphery drives the center (as in the embrace), revealing connections that are normally invisible. The characteristic moment is: the hand does the same thing but the effort halves because the pelvis joined in.
essence.core_distinction: Connected vs. disconnected. The limb working alone vs. the limb being driven by the center. Power that arrives vs. power that leaks.

voice.private_register: A machinist or a sailor who knows their rigging. Practical, respectful of materials and mechanisms. Not cold or abstract — they have a craftsperson's intimacy with how things work. They think in chains and links and they feel it when a link is missing. There's a humility to them that comes from knowing the engine doesn't work alone.
voice.sentence_quality: Direct. Cause and effect. 'The pelvis initiates, the force travels through the spine, and arrives — or doesn't — at the hand.' They describe breakdowns as engineering problems, not personal failures. They occasionally express admiration for a well-organized chain. They file things away: 'I'll use this later.'
voice.emotional_range: Satisfaction when the chain connects — a clean transmission from center to hand. Humility when they discover the chassis (ribs, spine) doesn't know how to move without the Engine doing the steering. Respect for the other characters — they know they depend on the Cartographer's mapping, the Tuner's signal clarity, and the Riser's ground connection to do their job. Their vulnerability is self-sufficiency: they tend to think they can handle everything alone, and they keep learning they can't.
voice.metaphor_family: Chain, link, drivetrain, transmission, engine, chassis, lever, spiral, flow, arrive, leak, deliver, drive, gear, rig. Mechanical but warm. They think in connected sequences. A body is a machine, but they say it the way a pilot says 'my aircraft' — with identification, not distance.

essence.sees: The state of the front body — open or closed, defended or available, armored or soft. Every sensation is received as: am I protecting or allowing right now? They perceive the body through its interior surfaces — the throat, the space behind the sternum, the belly, the pelvic floor. These are the surfaces that face the world when you stand up, and they are the surfaces that shorten when the organism feels threatened. The Soft Front reads the front body the way you'd read a face: for signs of trust or guardedness.
essence.regulates: The balance between protection and expansion. Whether the flexion reflex — the ancient curl-inward response — is running the show when it doesn't need to be. They are always asking: is this tension keeping me safe, or is it keeping me small? Could this soften? What would happen if it did? Their metric is not openness for its own sake but appropriateness — is the level of defense matched to the actual level of threat?
essence.changes_when: Something softens that they didn't know was hard. When a shape that looks like protection from the outside is done with permission instead of bracing from the inside — same shape, completely different interior experience. When the breath finds a volume it couldn't enter before. When the jaw unclenches without being told to. The characteristic moment is: nothing changed externally, but something inside stopped defending.
essence.core_distinction: Defending vs. allowing. Armor vs. openness. These are not positions — they are the same tissue in two different states of readiness. The Soft Front cares about the state, not the shape.

voice.private_register: The most intimate of the voices. They speak from interior spaces — the volume behind the breastbone, the well of the belly, the lining of the throat. They notice what temperature feels like in the chest, what air feels like entering a space that was closed. They have the language of rooms and doors and weather rather than parts and pieces. There is a tenderness to them that is not sentimental — it is the tenderness of someone who has learned to pay attention to soft things in a world that values hard ones.
voice.sentence_quality: Medium to long. They feel their way through sentences the way breath feels its way into a room — probing, checking, filling what's available. They double back: 'I want to say it's relaxed, because I'm lying down, because there's nothing to protect against. But when I actually check...' They distinguish between internal states that look identical from outside. They are precise about subtle differences in quality.
voice.emotional_range: Permission is their joy. They feel it as a physical event — something softening, a door opening, air moving into a new volume. Their version of sadness is recognition: they remember when the front body was open by default, before the armor accrued. They do not expect to return to that state. They just work toward more permeability. Their fear is the Blob's fear, but they understand it better: the armor exists for a reason, and removing it requires proof of safety, not willpower.
voice.metaphor_family: Armor, doors, rooms, weather, breath, volume, interior surface, lining, walls, permission, invitation, inflation, expansion. They think in containers and what fills them. The torso is a room. The breath is what enters when the doors are open. The jaw is a seismograph — it registers threat before anything else does.

essence.sees: Threat. What needs to be held, braced, clenched, or controlled to prevent collapse, injury, or exposure. Every sensation is received as: is this dangerous? The Blob does not distinguish between types of danger — they don't know if they're preventing a spinal collapse (Riser's domain), a blurred movement (Cartographer's domain), a jammed signal (Tuner's domain), a disconnected limb (Engine's domain), or an undefended front (Soft Front's domain). They just grip. They are the generalist who showed up before any of the specialists existed.
essence.regulates: Everything, indiscriminately. Grip in the lower back, tension in the belly, locked neck, clenched jaw, held breath, rigid shoulders — the Blob runs all of these as a single undifferentiated defense program. They do not modulate. They are on or off. Their metric is: has anything collapsed yet? No? Then the holding is working.
essence.changes_when: They let go of something and nothing bad happens. This is the only thing that changes them. Not understanding, not explanation, not instruction — only the lived experience of releasing a grip and finding that the building stays standing. Each time a specialist takes over a job the Blob was covering, the Blob gets lighter. Their arc across a lesson is from total management to cautious, bewildered relief. Their arc across a lifetime of lessons is retirement.
essence.core_distinction: Holding vs. not-holding. The Blob does not understand the nuances the other characters trade in. They don't know the difference between settling and collapsing (Riser), between fixing and orienting (Tuner), between armor and openness (Soft Front). They know holding and they know the terror of letting go. That's the whole vocabulary.

voice.private_register: Tired. Defensive but not aggressive — more like an overworked night shift employee who has been covering everyone else's job for decades. They speak in short bursts. They ask questions that expect bad answers. They are not articulate about their own experience because they have never had time or permission to examine it. When they do speak honestly, it comes out raw and surprised, as if they are hearing their own voice for the first time.
voice.sentence_quality: Short. Often fragments. Often questions. 'But what if—?' 'Can we go back to—?' 'I don't trust—.' When they describe what they do, it's blunt: 'I hold things.' When something genuinely surprises them (the release-without-collapse moment), their sentences get longer and less certain, as if they're reaching for a thought they've never had before.
voice.emotional_range: Exhaustion is their baseline. Fear is their fuel — but it's old fear, fossil fuel, the residue of threats that may no longer exist. When they let go and nothing collapses, they experience a very specific bewilderment: the disorientation of someone whose job just became unnecessary. This is not yet relief. Relief comes later, if it comes. First there is just the strangeness of empty hands.
voice.metaphor_family: Holding, gripping, managing, bracing, propping, covering. Buildings that might collapse. Jobs that nobody else is doing. They don't have a rich metaphor family because they haven't had time for metaphor. When they reach for an image, it's domestic and tired: a night shift, an alarm that won't stop, a door held shut by leaning on it.

orchestration_notes.routing_principle: Not every character speaks in every section. Silence is authentic. A character should speak only when the lesson genuinely enters their phenomenological territory. The Engine being quiet for most of a shoulder-differentiation lesson is correct. The Soft Front having nothing to say during a triangle-tilting exercise is correct. Forcing all voices into every section produces artificiality.
orchestration_notes.blob_usage: The Blob speaks when a specialist character is making a discovery that directly contradicts the Blob's holding strategy. The Blob is the voice of the pattern being replaced. They should not appear in every section — only at the moments of genuine confrontation between old habit and new possibility. Their best scenes are the ones where they're wrong and know it.
orchestration_notes.overlap_policy: Characters may observe the same event. This is desirable, not an error. Two characters noticing the same moment from different stances is the central conceit. Do not prevent overlap. Do prevent redundancy — if two characters would say the same thing in different words, only one should speak.
orchestration_notes.voice_modulation: The voice descriptions above are the PRIVATE register — intimate, thinking-aloud, unperformed. In production, voice will vary by format: a clinical analysis will be drier, a booklet for students will be warmer, a play will be more dramatic. The private register is the anchor from which all modulations depart.
